subject: Dedicated capacity: workload profile + recommended pool and pricing next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@solacethera.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:12:12-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing thought & next steps

Anna —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. I pulled together a short starting recommendation based on what we saw and a few quick follow-up questions to make the sizing quote accurate. Attaching a one-pager (Dedicated_pricing_summary_v1.pdf) with baseline economics.

Quick asks to finalize the proposal:
- Typical requests per minute (avg and 95th percentile) for the production chat endpoint.
- Avg/peak context length in tokens (and percent of sessions that exceed 8k tokens).
- Expected concurrency (long-running chat sessions vs short single-turn calls).
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95 token or response).

Based on the numbers from the demo, my initial recommendation for a 3–6 month reserved commit is a hybrid pool: 6 x A10G for steady-generation traffic + 2 x A100 for long-context jobs (batched long responses / reranking). That maps to a guaranteed throughput envelope of ~900–1,200 requests/min for your current model mix, with a burst buffer we can configure.

Pricing note: for a 6-month commit we typically price that configuration at list with a 15% commitment discount; larger or longer commits increase discount banding. I can loop in Marissa (SE) and Monica (Sales Ops) to convert this into a formal quote once you share the workload numbers.

If you prefer, we can design an elastic reserve (reserve base + monthly burst credits) that avoids overcommit for seasonal spikes.

Available windows for a short follow-up tech walk: Tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT or Thursday 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Dedicated_pricing_summary_v1.pdf
From: Anna Patel <anna@solacethera.com>

Date: 2026-10-06T11:03:43-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing thought & next steps

Thanks Marcus —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the docs. Answers inline below and I've attached our internal workload profile (Solace_Workload_Profile.xlsx).

- Avg requests/min (production chat): 220 rpm. P95 during business hours: ~1,150 rpm.
- Context length: median 600 tokens; ~18% of sessions > 6,000 tokens; ~4% > 12,000 tokens (these are long transcript summarization jobs).
- Concurrency: baseline 45 concurrent sessions, peak 180 concurrent (short spikes when campaign triggers).
- Latency SLO: p95 response < 700ms for user-facing chat; background summarization can be higher.

A few other asks:
- Can dedicated pools be split across regions (we have US + EU infra needs)?
- Do you support HIPAA controls / signing BAA?
- On pricing: we're targeting a spend profile where committed monthly spend is acceptable if discounting is meaningful — looking for ~25–35% off list for a 12mo commit.

Procurement copy: procurement@solacethera.com (please cc).

Best,
Anna
Anna Patel
Head of ML Platform | Solace Therapeutics
anna@solacethera.com

Anna —

Great detail — that's exactly what we needed. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Monica (sales ops) to convert this into a concrete sizing + pricing plan and to confirm security requirements (HIPAA/BAA).

Preliminary sizing notes from Marissa (high level):
- Baseline pool: 6 x A10G (handles short-turn chat & embeddings at low cost)
- Long-context lane: 2 x A100, configured for batched long summarization jobs (these are best-effort and run off a separate routing policy to avoid impacting chat latency)
- Autoscale / burst: Add an elastic buffer of +25% ephemeral capacity via burst credits for monthly spikes (~450–500 rpm buffer).

Estimated guaranteed throughput: 1,000 rpm (p95-target) with p95 response < 700ms for chat when the routing policy pins short-turn traffic to A10G pool. For the long-context flows we recommend asynchronous batching with a separate queue; that'll keep your user-facing SLO intact.

Pricing constructs to consider (Monica — feel free to edit):
- 12-month committed spend with quarterly true-ups: greater discount (target band study: 20–30% depending on commit size and region mix).
- Hybrid commit: base reserved commit (covers 70% of median usage) + monthly burst credits for seasonality. This avoids overpaying while giving predictable unit economics.
- Regional flexibility: we can allocate commit across US/EU pools with a single contract but different pool IDs — we'll need to size region splits to offer accurate pricing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to draft 2 pricing options (12mo/commit heavy, 12mo/hybrid base+burst) with line items and modeled cost per 1k requests.
2) Marissa to produce an SLO/routing map showing how long-context jobs will be routed to the A100 lane.
3) Schedule a procurement/technical call Wed 10/07 10:00 PT — does that work for you?

Marcus

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing thought & next steps

Thanks all — Wed 10/07 10:00 PT works. A couple of points ahead of the call:

1) Discounting: Solace is prepared to commit to a 12-month reserved agreement if we can land a 30%+ discount off list for the blended pool across regions. The business case needs predictable unit economics.
2) Regional flexibility: we need the ability to reallocate credits between US and EU on a quarterly cadence; otherwise we'll overcommit in one region. Can Redwood support that?
3) Security: HIPAA compliance is mandatory for parts of our workload. We will need the BAA + SOC2 Type II evidence.

Procurement will want a redlined SOW and a quote that separates base commit, burst credits, and one-time onboarding professional services. Please include credit terms and cancellation windows.

Anna

- Marissa will attach the SLO/routing diagram and an ops-runbook for the A100 long-context lane.
